vulkanmod.options.rayTracing.viewMode.to: Switches between the combined image, isolated RT terrain contributions, and Minecraft terrain without ray queries. Rasterization remains required for primary visibility.
vulkanmod.options.rayTracing.debugView.t: Replaces terrain shading with raw RT inputs or query results. Debug views temporarily force the ray-query terrain pipeline, even in Minecraft Only mode.
Sets the number of ray queries per shaded pixel. More rays make soft-shadow edges smoother but cost more GPU time.
vulkanmod.options.rayTracing.shadowSoftn: Controls the angular size of the ray-traced sun and the width of penumbras. Available when more than one shadow ray is used.
vulkanmod.options.rayTracing.shadowDarkn: Controls how much direct sunlight is removed inside a ray-traced shadow.
vulkanmod.options.rayTracing.shadowDista: Limits how far each shadow ray searches for an occluder. Lower values can reduce GPU cost but distant objects will not cast shadows.
vulkanmod.options.rayTracing.directLight: Separates sunlight, sky ambient and block light instead of applying RT shadows to Minecraft's completed lightmap.
vulkanmod.options.rayTracing.sunLight.to: Controls direct sunlight calculated from surface normals and ray-traced visibility.
vulkanmod.options.rayTracing.skyLight.to: Controls ambient illumination reaching terrain from the sky.
Controls the warm fallback illumination supplied by Minecraft's block-light level. Dynamic RT lights are added separately.
vulkanmod.options.rayTracing.dynamicLigh: Adds ray-query point lights for nearby emissive blocks and luminous items held by players.
Maximum number of camera-prioritized sources kept active. A spatial grid limits per-pixel evaluation to nearby cells. Very high values still increase CPU, upload and dense-scene GPU cost.
Camera radius used to select registered emissive blocks. Chunk builds maintain the registry, so distant searches do not scan every block each frame.
Traces one visibility ray toward every contributing dynamic light. Disabling this keeps light but removes its occlusion cost.
Controls the brightness of direct light from emissive blocks and held items.
vulkanmod.options.rayTracing.waterReflec: Traces one hardware ray from each visible water pixel to reflect terrain, foliage and the sky.
Controls the Fresnel-weighted amount of ray-traced reflection blended onto water.
Limits the distance searched by water reflection rays. Lower values reduce GPU cost and fade distant hits into the sky.
vulkanmod.options.performancePreset.tool: Applies a group of Minecraft and VulkanMod settings for the selected performance target.
vulkanmod.options.advCulling.tooltip: Use a culling algorithm that might improve performance by reducing the number of non visible chunk sections rendered.
vulkanmod.options.ao.subBlock.tooltip: ON (Sub-block): Enables smooth lighting for non full block (experimental).
vulkanmod.options.entityCulling.tooltip: Enables culling for entities on not visible sections.
vulkanmod.options.frameQueue.tooltip: Higher values might help stabilize frametime but will increase input lag.
vulkanmod.options.indirectDraw.tooltip: Reduces CPU overhead but increases GPU overhead. Enabling it might help in CPU limited systems.
vulkanmod.options.adaptiveChunkUploads.t: Adjusts chunk upload work from recent frame time to reduce stutter while moving or flying.
vulkanmod.options.uniqueOpaqueLayer.tool: Use a unique render layer for opaque terrain to improve performance.
vulkanmod.options.particleCulling.toolti: Cull redundant particles based on distance, player FOV, and maximum same-type count budgets.
vulkanmod.options.blockEntityCulling.too: Cull block entities (chests, signs, spawners, etc.) that are outside the camera frustum or further than 96 blocks.
vulkanmod.options.leavesCulling.tooltip: Cull adjacent interior faces of leaf blocks to significantly improve performance in forests.
vulkanmod.options.renderScale.tooltip: Renders Minecraft at a lower internal resolution, then scales it back to the current window or fullscreen size.
